rationale: Hand-written anchor-and-verify tactic for 'X and Y' hunts: enumerate the more listable condition from list pages, then verify the other condition per candidate with cheap batched checks.
instructions:
Every hunt asks for items meeting condition X AND condition Y.
1. Recall: write down every item you already know or suspect meets both conditions. These are free candidates; none is trusted until verified.
2. Size the target: search once for how many items exist (e.g. 'how many ... have won both', 'list of ...'). Note the expected count so you know when you are done.
3. Intersection page first: search for a page that lists the intersection directly (e.g. 'novels that won both Hugo and Nebula', 'physician astronauts'). If one exists, fetch it; it can replace step 4.
4. Otherwise anchor: pick the condition that is easier to list completely (an award's winners, an architect's works). Enumerate it from list and category pages, with query variants in one batch via 'also'. Fetch the most complete list page and extract every candidate.
5. Verify the other condition: send all unverified candidates (recalled and enumerated) to check_candidates with the filter condition as search words. Keep a candidate only when a result clearly shows it meets the filter.
6. If you are below the expected count, enumerate from a second, differently phrased source and verify the new candidates too.
7. Submit only verified items. Each find must cite a URL you actually retrieved in this attempt (a search result, a check_candidates result or a fetched page) that shows the second condition; finds without one score as wrong. Never submit items that meet only one condition.

For event hunts ("every time X happened with Y"), anchor on lists already sorted by the numeric or date condition ('deadliest ...', 'largest ...', '... by year'), then verify the number or date on each event's own page, because list pages disagree on counts.
routing_rules: Use exa for semantic list discovery ('list of ...'), brave for exact names and category pages. Restrict to en.wikipedia.org with include_domains when looking for list or category pages. Use the cheap verify route for check_candidates.
fetch_policy: Fetch list pages during enumeration. Do not fetch pages for single-candidate verification unless the check results are ambiguous.
